answer: Collective Budget Pools. Each agent draws from a shared per-task budget; coordination consumes it, so N coordinated identities deplete the pool N times faster than one. The pool refills only at a sable rate tied to verified task throughput. Attacker cost is linear depletion: each extra identity drains nectar from the same pool, forcing real work to fund it. A knoll of idle accounts starves the group, making mass coordination economically self-limiting.
